First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot {3}^{7x+2} & \le 2x\cdot {3}^{7x+3} \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {3}^{7x+2}-2x\cdot {3}^{7x+3} & \le 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2x\cdot 3)\cdot {3}^{7x+2} & \le 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-6x)\cdot {3}^{7x+2} & \le 0 \\ x(x-6)\cdot {3}^{7x+2} & \le 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${3}^{7x+2}$ and get

$$
x(x-6)\le 0.
$$

This represents an upwards parabola whose roots are at $x=0$ and $x=6.$ The parabola is below the $x$-axis or touch this axis when $0\le x\le 6.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013930/assets/d75b387ac3e54f253eab62d9492b39f2744298e776f663d542b26e3c47f7d6a9.png)

Therefore, the solution is $0\le x\le 6.$
